Requestor: Oyunbileg Batbayar
Requestee: Nikolaos Papadopoulos
Verdict: Approved
TechDebt: `parse_all` wraps each adapter in `except Exception` and returns normally, so the new `SanadsetSchemaError` family degrades a loud raise back into a quiet zero-row source — file a follow-up to make schema errors fatal there.

Reviewed at head `cb2f4c2a3c9074ad4e1afb5f0a1af04236d88ffa`, reading the artifact via `git show pr/359:<path>` against `git show origin/main:<path>`. I did not trust the description; every claim below was re-derived from the code.

## The new assertions are genuinely red against `main`

I executed `origin/main:src/parse/identity.py` in isolation (stubbing `src.models.enums`) rather than reasoning about it:

| input | `main` (pre) | head (post) |
|---|---|---|
| `lk:lk:1` | `hdt:lk:1` | raises |
| `sanadset:sanadset:0:0:2326` | `hdt:sanadset:0:0:2326` | raises |
| `sunnah:sunnah:bukhari:1` | `hdt:sunnah:bukhari:1` | raises |
| `hdt:sunnah:bukhari:1` | unchanged | unchanged |

`main` collapses and cannot raise, so every `pytest.raises(DoubledCorpusPrefixError)` case is behaviorally red there — not an `ImportError` artifact. Confirmed for the `identity.py` set specifically.

Four added tests do pass unchanged against `main`, and all four are deliberate controls that must be green on both sides — `test_does_not_flag_legit_repeat_deeper`, `test_does_not_flag_non_corpus_lead`, `test_bare_source_id_strips_hdt_prefix`, and the renamed `test_prefixed_and_bare_shapes_of_one_hadith_load_one_node`. Two more, `test_error_is_a_valueerror` and `test_schema_errors_are_named_and_are_valueerrors`, are definitional rather than behavioral. Separately, the missing-`Book`-column raise already existed on `main` as a bare `ValueError`, so da#358(c) narrows an existing guard's type rather than adding one. Worth stating plainly since the summary reads as if it were new.

## The blank-book fixture is not a toy

`test_blank_book_cell_raises_and_never_yields_doubled_id` writes `raw_dir / "sanadset.csv"` — the production filename — with a blank `Book` cell and `Num_hadith=645817`. On `main` that routes through `default_name = csv_file.stem.lower()`, which equals the corpus, producing `sanadset:sanadset:645817`. The bad id is genuinely reachable from this fixture, so the assertion is not structurally inert. This is the discipline that was missing last time.

Two small things. The production header is `Hadith,Book,Num_hadith,Matn,Sanad,Sanad_Length`; the fixture uses a prefix subset plus a `grade` column. Immaterial, since the parser regexes sanad/matn out of the `Hadith` field — but the "production header verbatim" claim is slightly stronger than the code. And the `_never_yields_doubled_id` half of the test name is never positively asserted; only the raise is. Fine in substance, since a raise emits no id.

## `lk:lk:1` and `sanadset:sanadset:` are safe — the highest-risk case clears

I audited every `generate_source_id` call site in `src/parse/` for a producer that can emit collection == corpus:

- `lk` maps filenames/dirnames to `bukhari`, `muslim`, `abu_dawud`, `tirmidhi`, `nasai`, `ibn_majah`. Never `lk`.
- `sanadset` keys the collection on the `_book_key` content digest. The CSV-stem `default_name` is now unreachable — a blank cell and a missing column both raise.
- `bihar-al-anwar`, `sahih_muslim`, `tahdhib-al-ahkam` / `al-istibsar`, thaqalayn's `bookId`, and the sunnah/fawaz/open_hadith/halimbahae book slugs are all structurally incapable of equalling their corpus.

Crucially, `validate_source_id` has *always* listed a doubled leading corpus as a contract violation. So `lk:lk:1` is not legitimate under the grammar — the raise did not replace "silently eat a valid segment" with "hard-fail on a valid segment", because there is no valid segment to eat. And da#353 (#357) merged 2026-07-09, so the "no producer emits this form" premise is true on `main` today rather than pending.

One correction to the prose. The `bare_source_id` docstring calls `lk:lk:1` "a collection legitimately named after its corpus" while the function rejects it and `validate_source_id` flags it. The behavior is right; the wording asserts a legitimacy the contract denies, and it is the sentence most likely to make a future reader reintroduce the collapse. Please reword.

One operational precondition for the team, not a change request. The currently-published pre-da#353 staging parquet **does** contain `sanadset:sanadset:<num>` ids. Loading that artifact under this code aborts the load. The imminent plan re-runs from `parse`, which regenerates staging with digest collections, so this is satisfied — but the wipe-and-reload must not be pointed at the existing artifact.

## `migrate.py` earns its place

It is reachable (`src/cli.py:311`, `_cmd_migrate_transmitted_hadith_ids`), tested (five new cases), and — importantly — it was *mandatory*, not speculative. On `main`, `compute_rewrites` called `hadith_node_id(raw)`; after this change that would raise on exactly the legacy ids the migration exists to repair. Decoupling it was forced.

I checked the property that actually matters for a migration, which the tests assert only pointwise. Legacy graph node ids were minted by the old `hadith_node_id`, so edge values must canonicalize identically. I verified `canonicalize_legacy_hadith_id` is byte-identical to `main`'s `hadith_node_id` across all nine probe inputs — triple corpus, non-corpus lead, repeated deeper segment, already-canonical, and the `hdt:`-prefixed forms. It is. That makes the migration correct rather than merely plausible, and it is idempotent, so it is a no-op on a rebuilt graph.

`test_migration_repairs_what_the_id_constructor_now_rejects` is the right test to have written — it pins the constructor/migration coupling that a future refactor would otherwise silently break.

The docstring narrows the precondition to legacy ids "whose collection segment was `0`", but the code also correctly handles the `sanadset:sanadset:<num>` stem-fallback shape. Under-inclusive prose over correct code.

## Raising does not abort a long stage, but it does hit a swallow

`src/parse/__init__.py::parse_all` wraps each adapter in `except Exception`, logs `parse_failed`, sets `results[name] = []`, prints `[FAIL]`, and returns normally — no re-raise, no nonzero exit. So a single bad row cannot kill the run. It also means a `BlankBookCellError` would drop all 650,986 sanadset hadiths and let resolve and load proceed against a silently empty source. That is the same failure class this PR was written to eliminate, one layer up. The swallow predates this change and blank `Book` is 0/650,986 on the real corpus, so it is not a blocker — but the PR routes new raises into it, and that is the tech-debt line above.

At load time the raising constructors are called per row in `load_nodes`, `load_edges`, and `composition` with no guard, so a doubled id aborts the load with zero nodes written. That is intentional and is what the integration test asserts. The ~7.5h resolve stage does not call these constructors, so there is no mid-run abort risk there.

CI is 7/7 green with a non-empty `statusCheckRollup`.

Nice work — the red-then-green discipline and the constructor/migration coupling test are exactly what this area needed after the inert-assertion incident.
